clue.text: Your address on Kipling's liner

definitions.meaning: the courteous way of speaking to a titled woman, as in 'Your ...'
Kipling's poem 'The Liner She's a Lady' makes the liner a lady's ship

explanation.surface: Someone writes to you aboard the ocean liner from a Kipling poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling wrote 'The Liner She's a Lady', so his liner is a lady's ship, split differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeress is addressed with this title, preceded by 'Your', just as a lord is 'Your Lordship'.

clue.text: Servant of the state coming up with the solution

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state
a key is the solution to a puzzle

explanation.surface: A government employee arrives bearing the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns CAL into LAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A footman or menial attendant, often used of a toady.

clue.text: Disparage unnatural diet range

indicators.note: unnatural means not in the normal state, so these letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Criticising a range of food as unnatural.
explanation.definitionFit: To belittle or criticise unfairly, to run down.

clue.text: Incomplete book reference to percolation

definitions.meaning: '...' with the number left off is a cross-reference that is unfinished
a slow leaking or oozing of liquid through a material

explanation.surface: A partial citation sends readers to an entry on filtering.
explanation.walkthrough: A book's cross-reference reads 'see page 12'; with no number it is incomplete. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid slowly leaking through porous ground or a crack is this, much like percolating water.

clue.text: Fashionable place for supply of computers

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
to put is to place

explanation.surface: A trendy spot sells computer supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Data fed into a computer is what it is supplied with.

clue.text: Melancholy effect of organ

definitions.meaning: ill humour or gloom, once thought to come from one bodily organ
the abdominal organ beside the stomach that filters blood

explanation.surface: A dark mood is blamed on some bodily part.
explanation.walkthrough: Old medicine held that this organ produced black bile, hence the mood sense; 'effect of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad temper and gloom were attributed to this blood-filtering body part, so its name came to mean the mood too.

clue.text: Tool to choose on river

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another comes first

parts.note: to pick is to choose
the Axe is a river in south-west England

explanation.surface: An instrument for selecting things beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Axe is a river in Devon and Dorset; 'on' puts PICK above AXE in the down grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy digging implement with a pointed iron head on a long handle.

clue.text: Triumph achieved late last month

parts.note: ex means former, late
ult., ultimo, is old business shorthand for last month

explanation.surface: Victory was won late last month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Triumph' looks like a noun but is the verb, to rejoice in victory.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoice exultantly, to celebrate a victory.

clue.text: What the judge does with currency receiver

definitions.meaning: a judge makes notes of the case before him
a wallet for banknotes

explanation.surface: A judge's handling of a cash wallet.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words: the judge notes the case.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallet or pocketbook for holding paper money.

clue.text: Catherine's favourite naval unit

definitions.meaning: Grigory, the lover and minister of Catherine the Great of Russia
a warship, the battleship famous for its 1905 mutiny

explanation.surface: Catherine's pet among the fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Russian battleship named after him mutinied in 1905, the subject of Eisenstein's film.
explanation.definitionFit: The prince who was Catherine the Great's lover and the battleship named for him share this name.

clue.text: Scorn Hampton's offence

parts.note: contempt is scorn or disdain
Hampton's, read as 'of Hampton', points to Hampton Court, so 'of court'

explanation.surface: Disdain for someone named Hampton counts as a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: HAMPTON COURT is a Tudor royal palace near London; 'Hampton's' is read as belonging to that Court.
explanation.definitionFit: Disobeying or disrespecting a judge or the proceedings is a punishable legal wrong.

clue.text: To proceed by cutting into stock points to corruption

definitions.text: To proceed by cutting into stock

parts.note: E and N are two compass points, east and north
graft is bribery or corrupt dealing

explanation.surface: A gardener's method of cutting into rootstock is linked somehow to corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the gardener's technique of inserting a shoot into a cut in rootstock.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners insert a scion into a slit in rootstock to join the two plants, which is exactly this verb.

clue.text: Adaptable compound of salt and ice

indicators.note: a chemical compound combines ingredients, so the letters of the two words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Something flexible is a chemical blend of salt and ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound of' mixes SALT and ICE; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flexible and able to stretch to fit circumstances is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Old dance is child's play

definitions.meaning: a strutting dance of the late nineteenth century, with a prize for the best walker
something very easy, a walkover

explanation.surface: A historic dance turns out to be easy.
explanation.definitionFit: The cake prize dance of old gave its name to anything won with no effort, a walkover.

clue.text: Contradiction in law to many in trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Legal conflict causes difficulty for many people.
explanation.definitionFit: A conflict between two laws or principles that both seem valid is a paradox in jurisprudence.

clue.text: Those changes to moral character

indicators.note: the word 'changes' tells us the letters of Those are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Some people alter their moral character.
explanation.definitionFit: The guiding beliefs and spirit of a person or community are its distinctive set of values.

clue.text: Sort of wisdom deer-stalkers may gain ?

definitions.text: Sort of wisdom deer-stalkers may gain ?

parts.words: Sort of wisdom deer-stalkers may gain ?
parts.note: wisdom after the event, read jokingly as hunters spotting a female deer

explanation.surface: Hunters learn something from stalking.
explanation.walkthrough: A hind is a female deer, so stalkers may catch a sight of one.
explanation.definitionFit: Understanding of events only after they have happened, wisdom after the fact.

clue.text: Top gear worn and antiquated? Keep it under your hat

definitions.text: Top gear worn and antiquated? Keep it under your hat

parts.words: Top gear worn and antiquated? Keep it under your hat
parts.note: an old-fashioned headpiece of false hair, worn literally beneath a hat, while 'keep it under your hat' means keep it secret

explanation.surface: Advice to keep quiet about wearing worn-out, dated clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR split 'anti-quated' at the line break. 'Top gear' is headwear, not a car's gear.
explanation.definitionFit: This French word names a periwig, the false hair men wore in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Opt for another name for Korea

definitions.meaning: to choose, as a verb
Chosen was Korea's old name, and chosen means picked or selected

explanation.surface: Choose an alternative name for the Korean peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: Korea was once called Chosen; that word also means picked, a sense this adjective shares ('the chosen few').
explanation.definitionFit: To choose by vote, and as an adjective meaning picked out, matching the old Korean name Chosen.

clue.text: Huge bird one can cut in pieces

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: cut into pieces means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A big bird can slice one up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut in pieces' turns I and CAN into ANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Of colossal size, like the giant Titans of Greek myth.

clue.text: Sound as a bell after a loss? Sensation!

indicators.note: after the loss of a letter, the 'a' is dropped from the bell's sound

parts.note: ting-a-ling is the sound a small bell makes

explanation.surface: Someone, healthy again after a defeat, makes a big impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound as a bell' looks like 'perfectly healthy' but is the noise TING-A-LING; with 'a loss' its A goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickling or stinging feeling in the skin is a physical sensation of this kind.

clue.text: They loiter about on foot

definitions.meaning: idlers who hang around doing nothing
slip-on shoes worn on the feet

explanation.surface: People hang around while walking.
explanation.definitionFit: Idlers who laze about share a name with casual slip-on shoes.

clue.text: Sky so bright, but pitch-black below the Pole

indicators.note: in a down clue, the second piece sits below the first

parts.note: S is the South Pole
tarry means black as pitch, covered in tar

explanation.surface: A clear night sky becomes dark beneath the pole star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Pole' wants to be the Pole Star; it is S for south.
explanation.definitionFit: A night sky full of shining stars is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Apple wife's not back

parts.note: Eve was made from Adam's rib, so a wife is a rib in crossword language

indicators.note: 'back' tells us the word not is read from end to start

explanation.surface: A wife says the apple is not to be returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NOT into TON. RIBSTON pippin is an old English apple variety.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ribston Pippin is an English dessert apple variety from Yorkshire.

clue.text: Goose seen in Greater London

definitions.meaning: a small dark wild goose
a north-west London borough

explanation.surface: A wild bird is spotted in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: BRENT is a London borough, home of Wembley.
explanation.definitionFit: The brent goose is a small dark wildfowl, and the London borough shares its name.

clue.text: Passage where Venus comes across Phoebus?

definitions.meaning: a passing through or across, conveyance
Phoebus is the sun god, so this is the planet Venus crossing the sun's disc

explanation.surface: A goddess meets a god in a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: Phoebus Apollo is the sun; astronomers call the planet Venus crossing the sun's face its transit.
explanation.definitionFit: Movement through or across, as in astronomy when a planet passes in front of the solar disc.

clue.text: Russian newsmen have nothing for a poet

parts.note: TASS is the Russian news agency
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Moscow reporters have nothing for a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: TASSO is Torquato Tasso, the Italian Renaissance poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was the sixteenth-century Italian epic poet of Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: Courier from college dining hall could be Green

parts.note: Queen's is a college at both Oxford and Cambridge
a mess is where service personnel eat

indicators.note: 'could be' says the letters of Green might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A dispatch rider from a university dining room might be called Green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges GREEN as ENGER.
explanation.definitionFit: The diplomatic courier who carries confidential documents for the British Foreign Office bears this title.

clue.text: Lure EEC into trouble — no end of it!

indicators.note: 'trouble' suggests disorder, so the letters are stirred into a new order
with no end, the final letter of 'into' is lost

explanation.surface: Tempting the European Community into difficulty, with no end in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of it' cuts INTO to INT; 'trouble' mixes EEC with INT.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt or attract someone, as bait does a fish.

clue.text: Stays firm: Terry's wavering.

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: wavering means unsteady, so the letters of Terry's shift into another order

parts.note: the possessive S is counted as a letter here

explanation.surface: Terry won't commit, yet claims to stand firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' looks like a verb but is the noun: the stiffening in a corset. 'wavering' rearranges TERRYS as RSETRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays are the boned undergarments that make up this collective term for foundation garments.
